patient_case.prompt_question: A 1-year-old girl is brought to a neurologist due to increasing seizure frequency over the past 2 months. EEG reveals hypsarrhythmia with slow waves, multifocal spikes, and asynchrony. The patient exhibits infantile spasms and physical exam shows innumerable hypopigmented macules and an irregular, thickened plaque on the lower back. Which of the following is most strongly associated with this patient's condition? Options: A. Cardiac rhabdomyoma, B. Glaucoma, C. Optic glioma, D. Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia
patient_case.note: This prompt originates from a clinical scenario; diagnosis or management is to be inferred.

branch.condition: Analyze each option based on known pathophysiology, presentation, and clues
branch.interpretation: Comparison against tuberous sclerosis features including infantile spasms, hypsarrhythmia, hypopigmented macules (ash leaf spots), and shagreen patch

diagnostic_options.description: Benign cardiac tumors frequently associated with tuberous sclerosis
evidence_for: Tuberous sclerosis is classically linked to cardiac rhabdomyomas in infancy
evidence_against: None relevant in this clinical context

diagnostic_options.description: An ocular condition involving increased intraocular pressure
evidence_against: Glaucoma is not a typical feature of tuberous sclerosis; it is more associated with other phakomatoses

diagnostic_options.description: Tumor of the optic pathway typically associated with neurofibromatosis type 1
evidence_against: Optic gliomas are not characteristic of tuberous sclerosis

diagnostic_options.description: A bone disorder most commonly linked with McCune-Albright syndrome
evidence_against: This condition is not associated with the dermatologic and neurologic findings seen here

reasoning_tree.conclusion: The clinical features are indicative of tuberous sclerosis, making cardiac rhabdomyoma the most strongly associated finding with this condition.
